name: LE, Dai Trang

headline.note: The frozen official record establishes journalism from 1991 to 2008 and business ownership from 2014 to 2022. Public biographies separate early private community-newspaper work from ABC employment beginning around 1994, but do not establish exact transition dates, hours, leave or substantive full-time status. Nonprofit leadership, advisory and board service, party/campaign activity, elected office and study are excluded. Missing evidence, including the 2008–2014 employment gap and possible cancer-treatment interruption, is not zero.

career_spells.role: Factory work ironing branded T-shirts and assembling watches while a child refugee
career_spells.evidence_note: In a first-person ABC account, Le states that she left the Hong Kong refugee camp each day to work in a factory, ironing branded T-shirts and assembling watches, when she was ten. The employer, pay, exact dates, hours and coercive circumstances are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: The work is retained as career-history evidence but cannot be classified or counted as documented adult full-time employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: The secondary synthesis, citing public profiles, identifies the degree and major but supplies no enrolment dates, load or overlap with early journalism.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liverpool City Champion and Fairfield City Champion (Fairfax Community Media network)
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen extract records journalism from 1991 to 2008. Le's own account says she began at the Liverpool City Champion, helped establish the Fairfield City Champion and then moved into an ABC researcher role. Secondary reporting places the newspaper start in 1990 and ABC commencement in 1994, creating a one-year discrepancy with the frozen start. Exact transition dates, hours, leave and employment terms are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private newspaper employment is supported, but year-boundary conflict and missing substantive full-time evidence prevent a headline duration.

career_spells.role: Researcher, journalist, film-maker, reporter, producer and broadcaster
career_spells.evidence_note: Le's current biography describes progression from an ABC researcher role into reporting and broadcasting. An archived Australia Vietnam Leadership Dialogue profile calls her a former ABC journalist, film-maker and broadcaster; secondary synthesis reports ABC service from 1994 to 2008 across television and radio. The frozen extract confirms the overall journalism endpoint in 2008, but exact start/end dates, hours, appointment basis, leave and internal role transitions remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: ABC is government-controlled, but a long professional career and senior duties do not alone establish a countable full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: Vincent Fairfax Ethics and Leadership Fellowship Program
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary synthesis reports selection for the 1996–1997 fellowship and travel during the program. It does not establish employment, hours or how the fellowship overlapped ABC work.
career_spells.counting_note: Professional development/fellowship activity is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.evidence_note: Member and secondary accounts identify Le as the Liberal candidate at the 18 October 2008 by-election. The nomination date, remuneration, campaign hours and relationship to the end of ABC employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.role: Candidate for Cabramatta at the NSW election
career_spells.evidence_note: ABC and secondary accounts identify a second Liberal candidacy at the 26 March 2011 state election. The nomination date, remuneration, campaign hours and any concurrent employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Multicultural NSW (formerly NSW Community Relations Commission)
career_spells.evidence_note: Archived organisational and secondary profiles report appointment to the state-government advisory board in August 2012. The end date, remuneration and workload are unresolved; advisory governance is not assumed to be employment.
career_spells.counting_note: Government advisory-board service is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.role: Councillor for Cabravale Ward, then Fairfield/Cabravale Ward
career_spells.evidence_note: The Fairfield heritage record and member biography corroborate council service since 2012; secondary election chronology supplies 9 September 2012 and the 4 December 2021 ward transition. The office continued after federal election and was current at the frozen snapshot.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Unidentified business venture(s), associated publicly with media and leadership initiatives
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract provides only 'Business owner from 2014 to 2022'. Public biographies identify several DAWN/media, leadership and entrepreneurial initiatives but do not reliably identify which legal entity or activity the official business-owner interval denotes. Hours, revenue/remuneration, leave, exact boundaries and overlap with cancer treatment, council and governance roles are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Business ownership does not by itself prove self-employment or substantive full-time work.

career_spells.evidence_note: An archived Australia Vietnam Leadership Dialogue profile identifies Le as founder and CEO and explicitly describes DAWN as a nonprofit association; a 2016 ABC author note corroborates her as founder. Exact formation/cessation dates, remuneration, hours and relationship to the frozen business-owner spell are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit leadership is displayed separately and excluded from the narrow public/private employment headline.

career_spells.employer: NSW Service for the Treatment and Rehabilitation of Torture and Trauma Survivors (STARTTS)
career_spells.evidence_note: The archived 2022 organisation profile reports directorship but gives no dates, remuneration, workload or operational employment relationship.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit board governance is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: The archived 2022 organisation profile reports the Deputy Chair title but gives no dates, remuneration, workload or operational employment relationship.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit governance is excluded from the narrow employment headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary chronology cites Fairfield City Council minutes for election on 21 December 2021 and records the term ending 27 September 2022. This office was nested within the councillor term and overlapped federal service after May 2022.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: ABC contemporary reporting and secondary chronology identify Le as the independent candidate elected on 21 May 2022. Nomination date, campaign remuneration and overlap with business, council and nonprofit activity are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Candidacy and campaign activity are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Fowler
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current member biography record House service from the 21 May 2022 election. Parliamentary responsibilities are nested within elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Western Sydney Community (formerly Dai Le & Frank Carbone Network)
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary chronology reports that Le and Frank Carbone founded the local political organisation in 2023. Remuneration, workload and exact date are unresolved; Le remained classified as Independent in the frozen federal roster.
career_spells.counting_note: Party-organisational activity is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary chronology cites Fairfield City Council minutes for re-election as Deputy Mayor on 8 October 2024. The office remained current at the frozen snapshot and overlaps both council and federal elected service.
career_spells.counting_note: Local elected office is excluded under the codebook.

sources.note: Secondary synthesis supplies the 1990/1994 employer sequence, degree, fellowship, precise elected-office dates and additional governance/party milestones, with underlying official and media citations. Primary follow-up remains necessary where the frozen record does not independently support dates.

research_notes: The frozen official 1991 journalism start is retained as the headline boundary for the first newspaper spell even though secondary reporting says the cadet role began in 1990; the discrepancy is explicit rather than silently resolved.
ABC is coded as a public corporation under government control, but no full-time duration is calculated because available biographies do not state hours or employment status.

The unidentified 2014–2022 business-owner spell is not conflated with DAWN: the available organisation profile describes DAWN as a nonprofit association, while the official extract does not name the business entity.
Council, deputy-mayor, party/campaign, advisory and board roles are displayed but excluded from the narrow employment headline.
Public sources do not establish whether 2014–2015 cancer treatment interrupted or reduced any business, council or nonprofit work.
open_questions: What were the exact start/end dates, hours, leave and employment terms at the Liverpool City Champion, Fairfield City Champion and ABC, and how should the 1990 versus 1991 start discrepancy be resolved?
What paid work, if any, occurred between leaving the ABC in 2008 and the official business-owner start in 2014?
Which legal entity and activities comprise the official 2014–2022 business-owner spell, and what were ownership, remuneration, hours, leave and exact boundaries?
Did cancer treatment in 2014–2015 create a break or reduced-hours interval in business or other work?
What were the dates, remuneration and workload for DAWN, Multicultural NSW, STARTTS, the Ethnic Communities Council and any DAWN Media Productions activity?
Were the 2008, 2011 or 2022 campaigns remunerated, and what employment overlapped those campaigns?
